## Decision

Decision ids D-24 through D-31 are AMBIGUOUS for this motive: they name different decisions in two disconnected stores. The JSONL store (.groundwork/journal/*.jsonl, read only by `bin/journal compile`) and the Markdown store (.groundwork/motives/obsidian-native-groundwork/decisions/*.md, read only by `gw journal compile` via bin/gw-hook) share no read path, so neither compiler can see or warn about the other's ids. Any future reference to a decision id in this range MUST name its store. New JSONL decision ids for this motive start at D-35 (D-32, D-33, D-34 are taken by this remediation).

## Rationale

Observed three times in this motive. (a) 2026-09-01T11:20Z: two agents independently appended different D-24 events; consolidated at 11:21Z. (b) 2026-09-01T14:26Z: a CLI root-resolution decision took D-25, shadowing the schema-staleness D-25 of 13:43Z; restored at 14:31Z and the displaced one re-recorded as D-28. (c) 2026-09-15T16:55Z: the vault-prohibition decisions, whose authoritative home is decisions/D-24.md and decisions/D-25.md, were appended to the JSONL store under those same ids with revises:"D-24"/"D-25", shadowing the check:pi decision (2026-09-02T04:22Z) and the restored schema-staleness decision. The mechanism is structural, not carelessness: `journal append` warns on an id collision, but the `revises` flag exists precisely to suppress that warning, and an agent copying an id across from the .md store has every reason to believe `revises` is correct — it is refining the decision it can see. The cross-store blindness is demonstrable: D-27 of this motive exists ONLY as decisions/D-27.md and never appears in `bin/journal compile` output at all, while the D-27 that DOES appear in the JSONL store belongs to a different motive (groundwork-development, session pacing). The compiled decision_log for this motive lists D-24 D-25 D-26 D-98 D-28 ... with D-27 simply missing. Recording this as a decision rather than leaving it in a charter note so it travels with the decision log itself, which is where the next agent will be standing when it hits the ambiguity.

## Alternatives Considered

- Renumber one store so ids are globally unique — rejected for now: renumbering the .md store rewrites authored files that other artifacts cite by id, and renumbering the JSONL store is prohibited by D-27 (append-only). A unifying read path across both stores is the real fix and is larger than this slice.
- Rely on the existing id-collision warning in `journal append` — rejected: the warning is cross-store-blind (it only sees JSONL ids) and is suppressed by `revises`, which is exactly the flag a cross-store copy invites.
- Document only in motive.md — rejected: an agent reading the compiled decision log does not necessarily read the charter; the ambiguity should be visible from inside the log.
